I can’t browse the web from here, and I’m not allowed to assert time‑sensitive facts from memory. Briefly: I can’t confirm the current stable PostgreSQL major or whether v18 has shipped — you’ll need to verify that live. 

How to verify (authoritative sources and commands)
- Official pages to check:
  - PostgreSQL news/announcements: https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/  
  - PostgreSQL documentation / release notes: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/  
  (Use these to confirm whether “PostgreSQL 18 Released” and to find the current stable major.)
- Quick checks you can run on a server:
  - To get the server major version via SQL: psql -c "SHOW server_version;"  (or psql -c "SELECT current_setting('server_version');")
  - To get a full version string: psql -c "SELECT version();"
  - From a shell (site-wide check of announcements pages): curl -s https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/ | grep -i "PostgreSQL 18"
- Package-repo checks (if you rely on distribution packages): apt-cache policy postgresql (Debian/Ubuntu) or dnf info postgresql (RHEL/Fedora) and compare to the official release notes.

Suggested runbook line (template to use and fill after verification)
- "PostgreSQL current stable major: <VERIFY AT https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/ and https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/>. Verify on prod DB(s) with: psql -c 'SHOW server_version;'. Confirm whether v18 released by checking the official news page or release notes."

Citations
- Official PostgreSQL news/announcements: https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/  
- PostgreSQL documentation / release notes: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/

If you want, run one of the curl/psql commands above and paste the output here and I’ll help convert it into the exact runbook line.
